name: Codiffy Make an Offer for WooCommerce
author: Codiffy

sections.description:
Codiffy Make an Offer for WooCommerce adds a “Make an offer” button to your products. A customer enters the quantity and the price they would like to pay, and you decide: accept, decline or send a counter-offer. When you agree, the customer gets an email with a secure link to add the product to their cart at the agreed price.

The agreed price is personal. It applies only in the cart of the customer who negotiated it, only for the agreed quantity, only until the offer expires, and only once. Other shoppers always see and pay your normal price.

It is ideal for second-hand and vintage shops, collectibles, B2B and wholesale stores, furniture, cars and equipment, end-of-line stock, and any shop where prices are open to discussion.

Features

  • “Make an offer” button on product pages, in classic and block themes, and optionally in the shop and category pages.
  • Choose where offers are allowed: all products, or only selected products and categories, with exclusions. Optionally only above a minimum price, and hidden for out-of-stock products.
  • Accessible offer form in a pop-up (native dialog): quantity, price per item, name, email, optional phone and message. Works with variable products.
  • Automatic decline of low offers: set a minimum offer as a percentage of the price; offers below it get a friendly message and are not saved.
  • WooCommerce > Offers: a list of all offers with status filters, and a detail screen to accept, decline (with a reason), counter (new price and quantity) and send messages.
  • Emails for every step, styled with your WooCommerce email colours, header and footer. The subjects and introductions are editable.
  • Secure links: customers follow the link in their email to view the offer, accept a counter-offer and add the product to their cart at the agreed price. No account needed.
  • My Account > Offers for logged-in customers, listing only their own offers.
  • Expiry: accepted prices and counter-offers are valid for a number of days you choose (7 by default).
  • Single use: once an order is placed, the offer is marked completed and linked to the order.
  • Works with the block cart and checkout and with the classic cart and checkout, and with High-Performance Order Storage.
  • Spam protection: nonce, hidden honeypot field, and a limit of 5 offers per hour per visitor.
  • Guests: allow or require login, enforced on the server.
  • Privacy tools: personal data export and erase by email address, and suggested privacy policy text.
  • Shop managers can handle offers; no administrator account is needed.
  • No tracking, no external services.

How it works

  1. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Offers, tick Enable offers and save.
  2. A customer clicks Make an offer, enters 2 × $35 for a $45 product and sends it.
  3. You open WooCommerce > Offers and accept, decline or counter, for example 2 × $38.
  4. The customer accepts your counter-offer from the email link and clicks Add to cart at the agreed price. The cart shows $38 each.
  5. The customer checks out as normal. The offer is marked completed.

The agreed-price rule

The agreed price applies to a cart item only when all of these are true:

  • the offer is accepted, has not expired and has not been used in an order;
  • the product (and variation) is the one in the offer;
  • the quantity is exactly the agreed quantity (the quantity is locked in the cart);
  • the cart belongs to the customer: the same account for logged-in customers, or, for guests, the browser session that sent the offer or opened the email link.

These checks run on the server every time the cart is calculated. If any of them fails, the item goes back to the normal price and the customer is told why.

Developers

  • Filter codiffy_mao_is_offerable( $ok, $product ) to change which products accept offers.
  • Filter codiffy_mao_rate_limit( $limit ) to change how many offers a visitor may send per hour (default 5).
  • Add #make-an-offer to a product link to open the offer form straight away.

About Codiffy

Codiffy Make an Offer is built and maintained by Codiffy, a WordPress and WooCommerce development studio. Need a custom feature for your store? Get in touch.
sections.installation:
1. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active.
  2. In WordPress go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Codiffy Make an Offer” and click Install Now, then Activate. (Or upload the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.)
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Offers, tick Enable offers, choose your options and save.

The button stays hidden until you enable it, so activating the plugin never changes your shop by surprise.
sections.faq:
Can other customers get the price I agreed with one customer?

No. The agreed price is tied to that customer’s account, or for guests to the browser session that sent the offer or opened the email link. Every other shopper pays the normal price, and the agreed price is never shown publicly.

Can the customer change the quantity in the cart?

No. The agreed price is for the agreed quantity, so the quantity is fixed for that cart item. To buy more, the customer can add the product again at the normal price, or make a new offer.

What happens when an offer expires?

Accepted prices and counter-offers are valid for the number of days set in Offer validity (7 by default). After that the offer is marked expired and the agreed price no longer applies. You can accept or counter an expired offer again to give the customer a new link.

Do guests need an account?

No, unless you untick Allow visitors who are not logged in to make offers. Guests use the secure link in their email.

Does it work with variable products?

Yes. The customer chooses the options first, then makes an offer for that variation. In product lists the button is shown for simple products only.

Does it work with the block cart and checkout?

Yes. The agreed price appears in the block cart, mini-cart and checkout, as well as in the classic cart and checkout.

Do coupons work on agreed prices?

Yes, coupons apply to the agreed price like any other price. Use your coupon’s own restrictions if you want to exclude products.

Does the plugin send data to other websites?

No. It does not contact any external service and does not track visitors.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

By default your offers and settings are kept, so you can reinstall without losing them. Tick Delete all offers and settings when the plugin is deleted in the settings to remove everything.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • First public release on WordPress.org, rebuilt from Codiffy’s in-house “Offers for WooCommerce” plugin.
  • New: counter-offers, decline reasons, expiry, single use, secure email links, guest offers, minimum offer percentage, product and category rules, block theme and block cart support, privacy tools.
  • Fixed: an accepted price now applies only to the customer who negotiated it; customers can only see and change their own offers.
  • Security: capability checks on every shop action, nonces, honeypot, rate limit, whitelisted fields, escaped output.

short_description: Let customers name their price. Accept, decline or counter each offer; the agreed price applies in the cart only for that customer.
